analysis:
Integration reviewed all 13 units. The PR adds a 30s coordinator handshake deadline (CoordinatorConnectionHandshake, config.handshakeTimeout, CoordinatorError.handshakeTimeout), extracts connectionParameters(for:) unchanged from CoordinatorClient+Connection.swift, and lets performLifecycleDrain (ProviderLoop+Lifecycle.swift ~100-116) settle without a coordinator ack when hasRegisteredConnection() is false. The rest is docs: cli-reference.md, protocol-messages.md, telemetry-schema.md, and the changelog.

Drain change: the new predicate is evaluated only after the ack attempt did not succeed. Other drain conditions are unchanged (nativeOwnersDrained, lifecycleRemaining == 0, App Attest worker retired). coordinatorAcknowledged is still set only from the real ack, so telemetry stays honest. A registered session whose ack times out still yields a non-drained outcome, so the barrier for a registered session is preserved. No change to A-016/T-053 authorization, encryption (T-008), or the T-041 cache posture. The residual risk is a window where hasRegisteredConnection() returns false while the coordinator still sees a live session (reconnect race), which could lose a final usage or terminal message. The supplied evidence neither shows nor refutes this. hasRegisteredConnection() and CoordinatorClient session-state handling are not in the supplied source, so I record this as an unverified contract, not a finding.

Handshake: the patch lines I could see (the Connection.swift diff, plus the CoordinatorConnectionHandshake implementation described in the unit 11 analysis) show TLS selection by URL scheme unchanged and exactly-once continuation resumption described. The 30s deadline is an availability improvement for TB-002. The CoordinatorConnectionHandshake file itself is not in the visible integration source. The remaining checks are that the timeout cancels the NWConnection, that the defer cleanup (resume nonce, chunk batcher) still runs on timeout, and that a zero or negative handshakeTimeout is self-inflicted only. No security regression was identified; the handshake and drain-predicate source behind these claims could not be fully verified, so a deeper source check is warranted.
